morning_starts.title: Heart Coffee Roasters
morning_starts.note: Light-roast evangelists on Burnside; order it black and don't argue.

morning_starts.title: Coava Coffee Roasters
morning_starts.note: The bamboo-slat bar where I finally understood pour-over for the first time.

morning_starts.title: Stumptown Coffee Roasters (Division Street)
morning_starts.note: The one that started the whole Portland coffee arms race; still holds up.

morning_starts.title: Ken's Artisan Bakery
morning_starts.note: Get there before the morning buns sell out, because they will.

morning_starts.title: Little T American Baker
morning_starts.note: A proper croissant without the Ken's line out the door.

morning_starts.title: Water Avenue Coffee
morning_starts.note: Industrial-eastside roaster where the breakfast sandwich earns the walk.

morning_starts.title: Nossa Familia Coffee
morning_starts.note: Family Brazilian roaster; the cafe's an easy, unhurried place to start.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Forest Park & the Wildwood Trail
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Thirty miles of fern and Doug fir five minutes from downtown; this is why we tolerate the rain.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Mount Tabor Park
beach_lake_outdoor.note: An honest-to-god extinct volcano with a reservoir view; run the steps if you're feeling smug.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Sauvie Island Wildlife Area
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Beaches, berry U-pick, and sandhill cranes fifteen minutes north; leave your shoes in the car.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Multnomah Falls
beach_lake_outdoor.note: 620 feet of waterfall postcard 45 minutes out; go early or fight the whole Gorge for parking.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Hoyt Arboretum
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Twelve miles of trail through trees labeled so you can pretend you knew.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Springwater Corridor & Oaks Bottom Wildlife Refuge
beach_lake_outdoor.business: Springwater Corridor & Oaks Bottom Wildlife Refuge
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Flat riverside bike path past a heron rookery; the least dramatic, most repeatable outdoor day.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Powell Butte Nature Park
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Meadow-topped butte with a Cascade lineup on the rare clear day; the locals' quiet one.

culture_history.title: Portland Art Museum
culture_history.note: Oldest museum in the Northwest; the Native American wing alone is worth the ticket.

culture_history.title: Lan Su Chinese Garden
culture_history.note: A walled Ming-dynasty garden dropped into Old Town; get tea in the teahouse and slow down.

culture_history.title: Portland Japanese Garden
culture_history.note: Widely called the best outside Japan, and up in the West Hills it earns it.

culture_history.title: Pittock Mansion
culture_history.note: A lumber baron's chateau with the best standing view of the city and Mt. Hood.

culture_history.title: Oregon Historical Society Museum
culture_history.note: Where the whole strange Oregon story lives; it doesn't hide the exclusion laws.

culture_history.title: Portland Chinatown Museum
culture_history.note: Small, sharp, and the right first stop before you eat your way through the pods.

culture_history.title: Portland Saturday Market
culture_history.note: Under the Burnside Bridge since '74; the oldest continuous open-air market in the country.

shopping_browsing.title: Powell's City of Books
shopping_browsing.note: A full city block of books; bring a map and cancel your afternoon plans.

shopping_browsing.title: Music Millennium
shopping_browsing.note: Last of the great independent record stores; the staff picks are gospel.

shopping_browsing.title: Tender Loving Empire
shopping_browsing.note: Local-made everything with a record label attached; the gift problem is solved here.

shopping_browsing.title: Movie Madness
shopping_browsing.note: A working video store that's also a film-prop museum; yes, that's the actual knife.

shopping_browsing.title: Mississippi Records
shopping_browsing.note: Cramped vinyl temple with a reissue label; dig and you'll find the record.

shopping_browsing.title: Cargo
shopping_browsing.note: A warehouse of imported oddities you didn't know you needed until now.

shopping_browsing.title: Beam & Anchor
shopping_browsing.note: Handsome maker-goods shop over a working studio; browse slow, buy the one nice thing.

casual_lunch.title: Nong's Khao Man Gai
casual_lunch.note: One dish, chicken and rice, done so right she built an empire on it.

casual_lunch.title: Kim Jong Grillin'
casual_lunch.note: Korean rice bowls out of a cart on Division; the kimchi does the heavy lifting.

casual_lunch.title: Matt's BBQ
casual_lunch.note: Central-Texas brisket out of a trailer; go at noon or it's gone.

casual_lunch.title: Hawthorne Asylum
casual_lunch.note: A full cart pod with covered seating and a fire pit; everyone at the table gets what they want.

casual_lunch.title: Screen Door Eastside
casual_lunch.note: Southern comfort with the fried chicken everybody warned you about; worth the wait.

casual_lunch.title: Eem
casual_lunch.note: Thai barbecue from a cart-pod alumni team; the burnt-ends curry is the move.

casual_lunch.title: The Heist
casual_lunch.note: Solid cart pod when you want a covered seat and a beer with the meal.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Rum Club
happy_hour_drinks.note: Neighborhood tiki-adjacent bar; the Rum Club Daiquiri is the correct order.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Scotch Lodge
happy_hour_drinks.note: Below-grade whisky den on Belmont; dim, plush, dangerously easy to stay in.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Wayfinder Beer
happy_hour_drinks.note: Big lager-forward brewpub near the bridge; the pilsner and the burger, done.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Angel Face
happy_hour_drinks.note: No menu — you name a spirit and a mood and trust the bartender.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Palomar
happy_hour_drinks.note: Cuban-leaning cocktails on the eastside; the daiquiris and the crowd both hum.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Breakside Brewery
happy_hour_drinks.note: The IPA people who keep winning medals; get the flagship and a pretzel.

dinner_casual.title: Gado Gado
dinner_casual.note: Indonesian-American feast built for sharing; order too much on purpose.

dinner_casual.title: Han Oak
dinner_casual.note: Korean cooking in a converted courtyard home; the dumplings are family recipe.

dinner_casual.title: Navarre
dinner_casual.note: Order-by-checklist small plates, part French, part farm; regulars just say 'bring us food.'

dinner_casual.title: Kachka
dinner_casual.note: Russian zakuski and infused vodkas; loud, warm, and gloriously over-the-top.

dinner_casual.title: Screen Door Eastside
dinner_casual.note: Same Southern comfort, dinner edition, and the biscuits don't quit.

dinner_casual.title: Eem
dinner_casual.note: Thai barbecue and knockout cocktails; the room stays loud for a reason.

dinner_casual.title: Higgins Restaurant & Bar
dinner_casual.note: The farm-to-table original still doing it right; the bar menu is the low-key move.

dinner_upscale.title: Le Pigeon
dinner_upscale.note: Counter-seat fine dining; foie gras profiteroles and a beef cheek that made the reputation.

dinner_upscale.title: Nodoguro
dinner_upscale.note: Intimate Japanese tasting menu; book ahead, show up hungry, ask no questions.

dinner_upscale.title: Langbaan
dinner_upscale.note: Hidden Thai tasting room behind a restaurant; the toughest reservation in town, and worth it.

dinner_upscale.title: Ox
dinner_upscale.note: Argentine wood-grill; the grilled-clam chowder alone justifies the whole meal.

dinner_upscale.title: República
dinner_upscale.note: Modern Mexican tasting menu with masa milled in-house; ambitious, and it lands.

dinner_upscale.title: Kann
dinner_upscale.note: Gregory Gourdet's live-fire Haitian; James Beard-anointed and it earns every bit.

dinner_romantic.title: Coquine
dinner_romantic.note: Mount Tabor bistro that started as a pop-up; the smoked-chocolate chip cookie is the closer.

dinner_romantic.title: Jacqueline
dinner_romantic.note: Candlelit seafood on the eastside; oysters, natural wine, and low lighting doing their job.

dinner_romantic.title: St. Jack
dinner_romantic.note: Lyon-style bistro; steak frites, a Lyonnaise salad, and a booth for two.

dinner_romantic.title: Kann
dinner_romantic.note: Wood-fire warmth and island spice; ask for a two-top away from the pass.

dinner_romantic.title: Angel Face
dinner_romantic.note: Tuck into the little Alberta bar, order two bespoke cocktails, and let the night unfold.

dinner_romantic.title: Le Pigeon
dinner_romantic.note: The communal counter sounds unromantic until the beef cheek arrives and you stop talking.

nightlife.title: Crystal Ballroom
nightlife.note: Historic dance floor — literally sprung — where the touring acts still play.

nightlife.title: Roseland Theater
nightlife.note: Downtown mid-size room; the bill's always heavier than the marquee suggests.

nightlife.title: The Sandy Hut
nightlife.note: Beloved dive on Sandy; strong pours, pinball, zero pretense.

nightlife.title: The Yamhill Pub
nightlife.note: Grimy, cash-friendly downtown institution; you'll fit right in by the second round.

nightlife.title: Revolution Hall
nightlife.note: Old high-school auditorium turned venue; catch a show then hit the rooftop bar.

nightlife.title: Kachka
nightlife.note: Vodka flights until late; the party tends to find itself around midnight.

family_activities.title: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry (OMSI)
family_activities.business: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry (OMSI)
family_activities.note: Hands-on science, a planetarium, and a real submarine docked out back; a whole day disappears here.

family_activities.title: Oregon Zoo
family_activities.note: Up in Washington Park off the MAX line; the elephants are the marquee, the train's the win.

family_activities.title: Portland Aerial Tram
family_activities.note: A three-minute cable-car ride up to OHSU with a Mt. Hood payoff; kids lose their minds.

family_activities.title: Kerr Bikes (Wheel Fun Rentals) at Waterfront Park
family_activities.business: Kerr Bikes (Wheel Fun Rentals) at Waterfront Park
family_activities.note: Rent a surrey-cycle and pedal the waterfront loop; peak wholesome.

family_activities.title: Topaz Farm (formerly Kruger's Farm)
family_activities.note: Sauvie Island U-pick, animals, and weekend live music; bring a wagon.

family_activities.title: Portland Saturday Market
family_activities.note: Buskers, food carts, and made-here crafts under the bridge; free to wander.

family_activities.title: Tryon Creek State Natural Area
family_activities.note: Easy forested loops with a nature center; the trail your six-year-old can actually finish.

rainy_day.title: Powell's City of Books
rainy_day.note: A city block of books with coffee built in; the definitive Portland rainy day, full stop.

rainy_day.title: Portland Art Museum
rainy_day.note: Warm, dry, and deep; give the Native American and Northwest galleries a slow hour.

rainy_day.title: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry (OMSI)
rainy_day.business: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry (OMSI)
rainy_day.note: Planetarium, submarine, and enough hands-on exhibits to outlast any storm.

rainy_day.title: Lan Su Chinese Garden
rainy_day.note: Covered walkways ring the pond, so the rain becomes the whole point; tea in the teahouse seals it.

rainy_day.title: Movie Madness
rainy_day.note: 20,000 titles and a film-prop museum; the browse itself is the entertainment, umbrella optional.

rainy_day.title: Portland Chinatown Museum
rainy_day.note: Small enough to duck into, sharp enough to reframe Old Town before your cart crawl.

rainy_day.title: Oregon Historical Society Museum
rainy_day.note: Downtown, cavernous, full of the state's strange history — the ideal place to dry off and read walls.
